Options.dos2unix: Transform DOS or Windows guest output to UNIX or Linux output. This transformation changes CR + LF line endings to LF. Not yet implemented.
Options.unix2dos: Transform UNIX or Linux guest output to DOS or Windows output. This transformation changes LF line endings to CR + LF.
Options.dereference: Enables following of symbolic links on the guest file system.
Options.noreplace:
Only copies a file if it does not exist on the host yet.

The short form of this option is -n.
Options.recursive:
Recursively copies files and directories from the specified guest directory to the host.

The short form of this option is -R.
Options.targetdirectory: Specifies the absolute path of the destination directory on the host system. For example, C:\Temp.
Options.update:
Only copies a file if the guest file is newer than on the host.

The short form of this option is -u.
Options.humanreadable: Shows the disk sizes in a human readable form.
Options.total: Produces a grand total of all disk sizes.
Options.parents:
Creates any of the missing parent directories of the specified directory.

For example, if you attempt to create the D:\Foo\Bar directory and the D:\Foo directory does not exist, using the --parents creates the missing D:\Foo directory. However, if you attempt to create the D:\Foo\Bar and do not specify the --parents option, the command fails.
Options.mode: Specifies the permission mode to use for the specified directory. If you specify the --parents option, the mode is used for the associated parent directories, as well. <mode> is a four-digit octal mode such as 0755.
Options.force:
Forces the operation and overrides any confirmation requests.

The short form of this option is -f.
Options.directory: Creates a temporary directory that is specified by the <template> operand.
Options.secure: Enforces secure file and directory creation by setting the permission mode to 0755. Any operation that cannot be performed securely fails.
Options.tmpdir: Specifies the absolute path of the directory on the guest VM in which to create the specified file or directory. If unspecified, <directory> is the platform-specific temp directory.
Options.sessionid: Specifies the ID of the guest session.
Options.sessionname: Specifies the name of the guest session. Use a pattern that contains wildcards to specify multiple sessions.
Options.source: Specifies the absolute path of the Guest Additions update .ISO file on the guest VM.
Options.reboot: Automatically reboots the guest after a successful Guest Additions update.
Options.verify: Verifies whether the Guest Additions were updated successfully after a successful installation. A guest reboot is mandatory.
Options.waitready: Waits for the current Guest Additions being ready to handle the Guest Additions update.
Options.waitstart:
Starts the VBoxManage update process on the guest VM and then waits for the Guest Additions update to begin before terminating the VBoxManage process.

By default, the VBoxManage command waits for the Guest Additions update to complete before it terminates. Use this option when a running VBoxManage process affects the interaction between the installer and the guest OS.

import.Summary: Import a virtual appliance in OVF format or from a cloud service and create virtual machines

Options.dryrun:
Performs a dry run of the VBoxManage import command instead of performing the actual import operation. A dry run operation does the following:

- Outputs a description of the appliance's contents based on the specified OVF or OVA file. - Shows how the appliance would be imported into Oracle VirtualBox. In addition, the output shows any options that you can use to change the import behavior.

The shortened form of this option is -n.
Options.options:
Enables you to fine-tune the import operation.

Valid arguments are as follows:

- keepallmacs: Specifies that the MAC addresses of every virtual network card are left unchanged. - keepnatmacs: Specifies that the MAC addresses of every virtual network card are left unchanged if the network type is NAT. - importtovdi: Specifies that all new disk images are to be created using the VDI file format. - keepextradata: Specifies whether extra data settings that may be present in the .ovf file are impor...
Options.ostype: Specifies the guest operating system (OS) information for the VM. Use the VBoxManage list ostypes command to view the OS type identifiers.
Options.vmname: Specifies the name for the imported VM to be used by Oracle VirtualBox.
Options.basefolder: Specifies the folder where the files of the imported VM are stored.
Options.memory: Specifies the memory size in Megabytes for the imported VM.
Options.cpus: Specifies the number of CPUs for the imported VM.
Options.description: Specifies the description text visible in the GUI and CLI when checking the VM details.
Options.vsys: Specifies the index selecting a specific VM within the appliance. Affects the following options.
Options.unit: Specifies the index selecting a specific unit of a VM within the appliance. Affects the following options.
Options.settingsfile: Specifies the filename (as a relative or absolute path) of the VM config file which will be created as part of the import. The preferred way to rename the settings file is to override the VM name using the --vmname option and if necessary specify the folder in which to create the VM with --basefolder.
Options.group: Specifies the primary group of the imported VM.
Options.eula:
Enables you to show or accept the license conditions of a VM within the appliance,

Valid arguments are as follows:

- show: Shows the EULA of a VM. - accepts: Accepts the EULA of a VM. Any VMs in an appliance which have an EULA require accepting it, otherwise the import will fail.
Options.ignore: Ignores the hardware associated with the VM specified with the --unit option when importing the VM, effectively removing all of its associated hardware.
Options.scsitype:
Enables you to select the type of the SCSI controller for the current unit of an imported VM.

Valid arguments are as follows:

- BusLogic: Uses the (very old) BusLogic SCSI controller type. - LsiLogic: Uses the (more modern) LsiLogic SCSI controller type.
Options.cloud: Specifies that the import should be from the cloud.
Options.cloudprofile: Specifies the cloud profile which is used to connect to the cloud service provider. The cloud profile contains your Oracle Cloud Infrastructure account details, such as your user OCID and the fingerprint for your public key. To use a cloud profile, you must have the required permissions on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.
Options.cloudinstanceid: Specifies the ID of an existing instance in the cloud.
Options.cloudbucket: Specifies the bucket name in which to store the object created from the instance. In Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, a bucket is a logical container for storing objects. By default the first bucket available with the cloud profile is used.

Options.autoreset: Specifies whether to automatically reset an immutable hard disk on every virtual machine (VM) startup. This option is only for immutable hard disks and the default value is on. See section "Special Image Write Modes" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.compact:
Compresses disk images by removing blocks that contain only zeroes. This option shrinks a dynamically allocated image and reduces the physical size of the image without affecting the logical size of the virtual disk.

You can use this option for base images and for differencing images that are created as part of a snapshot.

Before you compress the image, you must use a suitable software tool to zero out free space in the guest system. For example:

- Windows guests. Run the sdelete -z command....
Options.description: Specifies a text description of the medium.
Options.move: Specifies a relative or absolute path to a medium on the host system. Use this option to relocate a medium to a different location on the host system.
Options.property: Specifies a property name and value for the medium.
Options.resize:
Specifies the new capacity of an existing image in MB. You can use this option only to expand the capacity of an image. You can cannot shrink the capacity of an image.

Note that you can only resize dynamically allocated disk images that use the VDI and VHD formats. This option adjusts the logical size of a virtual disk and has only a minor affect on the physical size.

For example, if your dynamically allocated 10 GB disk is full, you can use the --resize 15360 option to increase the capacity o...
Options.resizebyte: Specifies the new capacity of an existing image in bytes. This option is similar to the --resize option, but you specify the size in bytes instead of megabytes.
Options.setlocation:

Note that the VBoxManage modifymedium command does not perform any sanity checks on the path name you specify. Ensure that the path name is valid.
Options.type: Specifies the new mode type of an existing image. Valid values are normal, immutable, writethrough, multiattach, shareable, and readonly. For descriptions of these mode types, see section "Special Image Write Modes" in chapter 1 of the user manual.

modifyvm.Summary: Change settings for a virtual machine that is stopped

Options.name: Changes the name of the VM and its related internal VM files. See "VBoxManage createvm".
Options.groups: Changes the group membership of a VM. Group names always begin with a slash character (/) and can be nested. By default, VMs are members of the / group. A VM can be member of multiple groups, but its primary group determines the directory structure where the internal VM files are placed by default.
Options.description: Changes the optional VM description. Use a description to record details about the VM in a meaningful way. The GUI interprets HTML markup while the VBoxManage modifyvm command enables you include arbitrary strings that can contain multiple lines.
Options.ostype: Specifies the guest operating system (OS) information for the VM. Use the VBoxManage list ostypes command to view the OS type identifiers.
Options.iconfile: Specifies the path to the VM icon file in PNG format on the host system. The icon is shown in the VM manager UI and when running the VM with UI.
Options.memory: Specifies the amount of host system RAM to allocate to the VM. The size is in MB. See chapter 1 "Creating a New Virtual Machine" in the user manual.
Options.pagefusion: Enables or disables the Page Fusion feature, which is disabled by default. Use the Page Fusion feature to minimize the memory duplication between VMs that have similar configurations and that run on the same host system. See section "Page Fusion" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.vram: Specifies the amount of RAM to allocate to the virtual graphics card. See section "Display Settings" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.acpi: Determines whether the VM has ACPI support. See section "Motherboard Tab" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.ioapic: Determines whether the VM has I/O APIC support. See section "Motherboard Tab" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.hardwareuuid: Specifies the Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) to present to the guest VM in memory tables (DMI/SMBIOS), hardware, and VM properties. By default this hardware UUID is the same as the VM UUID. Cloning a VM and the teleporting feature automatically preserve the hardware UUID value. Likewise for Virtual Appliance export and import, but only if both operations are done by Oracle VirtualBox.
Options.cpus:
Specifies the number of virtual CPUs to assign to the VM. See section "Processor Tab" in chapter 1 of the user manual.

If CPU hot-plugging is enabled, this option specifies the maximum number of virtual CPUs that can be plugged into the VMs.
Options.cpuhotplug: Enables or disables CPU hot-plugging. When enabled, you can dynamically add virtual CPUs to a VM or remove virtual CPUs from a VM. See section "CPU Hot-Plugging" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.plugcpu:
Adds a virtual CPU to the VM. <CPU-ID> is the index of the virtual CPU to add. A valid index value is a number from 0 to the maximum number of CPUs that you configured by using the --cpus option.

Only use this option if CPU hot-plugging is enabled.
Options.unplugcpu:
Removes a virtual CPU from the VM. <CPU-ID> is the index of the virtual CPU to remove. A valid index value is a number from 1 to the maximum number of CPUs that you configured by using the --cpus option.

Only use this option if CPU hot-plugging is enabled.

Note that you cannot remove CPU 0.
Options.cpuexectioncap:
Specifies how much CPU time a virtual CPU can use. A valid value is from 1 to 100. A value of 50 indicates that a single virtual CPU can use up to 50% of a single host CPU.

Use this feature with caution, it can have unexpected results including timekeeping problems and lower performance than specified. If you want to limit the resource usage of a VM it is more reliable to pick an appropriate number of VCPUs.
Options.pae: Enables or disables physical address extension (PAE). See section "Processor Tab" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.longmode: Enables or disables long mode. See section "Processor Tab" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.ibpbonvmexit: Enables use of Indirect Branch Prediction Barrier (IBPB) on every VM exit.
Options.ibpbonvmentry: Enables use of Indirect Branch Prediction Barrier (IBPB) on every VM entry.
Options.specctrl:
Enables or disables the exposure of speculation control interfaces to the guest VM. These interfaces must be available on the host system.

Depending on the host CPU and the workload, enabling speculation control might significantly reduce performance.
Options.l1dflushonsched: Enables or disables level 1 data cache flushing when a thread is scheduled to execute guest code. See section "CVE-2018-3646" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.l1dflushonvmentry: Enables or disables level 1 data cache flushing on every VM entry. See section "CVE-2018-3646" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.mdsclearonsched: Enables CPU buffer clearing when a thread is scheduled to execute guest code. See section "CVE-2018-12126, CVE-2018-12127, CVE-2018-12130, CVE-2019-11091" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.mdsclearonvmentry: Enables CPU buffer clearing on every VM entry. See section "CVE-2018-12126, CVE-2018-12127, CVE-2018-12130, CVE-2019-11091" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.cpuprofile: Specifies the profile to use for guest CPU emulation. Specify a value that is based on the host system CPU (host) or one of the following older Intel micro-architectures: 8086, 80286, or 80386.
Options.hpet: Enables or disables a High Precision Event Timer (HPET) that can replace a legacy system timer. This feature is disabled by default. Note HPET is supported on Windows versions starting with Vista.
Options.hwvirtex: Enables or disables the use of hardware virtualization extensions in the processor of the host system. Such extensions are Intel VT-x or AMD-V.
Options.triplefaultreset: Enables or disables the resetting of the guest VM instead of triggering a Guru Meditation. Some guest VMs raise a triple fault to reset the CPU, so sometimes resetting the guest VM is the best outcome. This option only applies to guests that do not use symmetric multiprocessing (SMP).
Options.apic: Enables or disables APIC. With APIC, OSes can use more than 16 interrupt requests (IRQs) to avoid IRQ sharing and to improve reliability. APIC is enabled by default. See section "Motherboard Tab" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.x2apic:
Enables or disables the CPU x2APIC feature. CPU x2APIC enables an OS to run more efficiently on high core count configurations and to optimize interrupt distribution in virtualized environments. This feature is enabled by default.

Disable this feature when the OS that runs on a host system or a guest VM is incompatible with CPU x2APIC.
Options.armgicits: Enables or disables the ITS (Interrupt Translation Service) component of the GIC (Generic Interrupt Controller). This feature is disabled by default.
Options.paravirtprovider:
Specifies one of the following paravirtualization interfaces to provide to the guest OS:

- none does not expose any paravirtualization interface. - default selects the appropriate interface based on the guest OS type when starting the VM. This is the default value used when creating new VMs. - legacy selects a paravirtual interface for VMs that were created by older Oracle VirtualBox versions. - minimal is required for Mac OS X guest VMs. - kvm is recommended for Linux guest VMs. See section "P...
Options.paravirtdebug: Specifies debugging properties that are specific to the paravirtualization provider configured for the specified VM. See section "Paravirtualized Debugging" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.nestedpaging: Enables or disables the nested paging feature in the processor of the host system. This option is available only when hardware virtualization is enabled. See section "CVE-2018-3646" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.largepages: Enables or disables the hypervisor's use of large pages, which can improve performance by up to 5%. The use of large pages reduces TLB use and overhead. This option is available only when both hardware virtualization and nested paging are enabled.
Options.vtxvpid: Enables or disables the use of the tagged TLB (VPID) feature in the processor of your host system. This option is available only when hardware virtualization is enabled on Intel VT-x.
Options.vtxux: Enables or disables the use of unrestricted guest mode for executing the guest VM. This option is available only when hardware virtualization is enabled on Intel VT-x.
Options.nestedhwvirt: Enables or disables nested virtualization. Enabling makes hardware virtualization features available to the VM. See section "Nested Virtualization" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.virtvmsavevmload: If hardware virtualization is enabled and the host has an AMD CPU, this setting enables or disables the use of the virtualized vmsave/vmload host feature while executing the VM. It is enabled by default. It is recommended to leave it enabled as it has a drastic impact on performance while executing nested VMs when using the nested hardware virtualization feature. section "Nested Virtualization" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.accelerate3d: Enables or disables hardware 3D acceleration for the graphics adapter variants which support it. This option has an effect only when the Guest Additions are installed. See section "Hardware-Accelerated Graphics" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.chipset:
Specify the Intel chipset for Oracle VirtualBox to emulate. For the x86 platform, the default value is the Intel PIIX3 chipset. (piix3). For the ARM platform, the default value is the ARMv8Virtual chipset. (armv8virtual).

Change this value only if you need to relax some of the chipset constraints. See section "Motherboard Tab" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.iommu:
Specifies the IOMMU type for Oracle VirtualBox to emulate. Both Intel and AMD IOMMU emulation currently require the use of the Intel ICH9 chipset (see --chipset option).

Valid values are as follows:

- none – No IOMMU is present and is the default value. - automatic – An IOMMU is present but its type is automatically chosen to match the host CPU vendor when the VM is powered on. - amd – An AMD IOMMU is present. - intel – An Intel IOMMU is present.
Options.tpmtype:
Specifies the TPM type for Oracle VirtualBox to emulate.

Valid values are as follows:

- none – No TPM is present and is the default value. - 1.2 – A TPM conforming to the TCG specification version 1.2 is present. - 2.0 – A TPM conforming to the TCG specification version 2.0 is present. - host – The host TPM is passed through to the guest. May not be available on all supported host platforms. - swtpm – The VM connects to an external TPM emulation compliant to swtpm. Requires to set the TPM loca...
Options.firmwarelogofadein: Specifies whether the BIOS logo fades in on VM startup. By default, an Oracle VirtualBox logo is shown.
Options.firmwarelogofadeout: Specifies whether the BIOS logo fades out on VM startup.
Options.firmwarelogodisplaytime: Specifies the amount of time in milliseconds that the BIOS logo is visible.
Options.firmwarelogoimagepath: Replaces the existing BIOS logo with a different image. The replacement image must be an uncompressed 16, 256 or 16M color bitmap file (BMP) that does not contain color space information (Windows 3.0 format). Also ensure that the image is no larger than 640 X 480 pixels.
Options.firmwarebootmenu:
Specifies whether the BIOS permits you to select a temporary boot device. Valid values are:

- disabled outputs the alternate boot device message and permits you to select a temporary boot device by pressing F12. - menuonly suppresses the alternate boot device message, but permits you to select a temporary boot device by pressing F12. - messageandmenu suppresses the alternate boot device message and prevents you from selecting a temporary boot device by pressing F12.
Options.firmwareapic:
Specifies the APIC level of the firmware. Valid values are: x2apic, apic, and disabled. When the value is disabled, neither the apic nor the x2apic version of the firmware is used.

Note that if you specify the x2apic value and x2APIC is unsupported by the virtual CPU, the APIC level downgrades to apic, if supported. Otherwise, the APIC level downgrades to disabled. Similarly, if you specify the apic value and APIC is unsupported by the virtual CPU, the APIC level downgrades to disabled.
Options.firmwaresystemtimeoffset: Specifies the time offset in milliseconds of the guest VM relative to the time on the host system. If the offset value is positive, the guest VM time runs ahead of the time on the host system.
Options.firmwarepxedebug: Enables or disables additional debugging output when using the Intel PXE boot ROM. The debug output is written to the release log file. See section "Collecting Debugging Information" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.systemuuidle: Enables or disables representing the system UUID in little endian form. The default value is on for new VMs. For old VMs the setting is off to keep the content of the DMI/SMBIOS table unchanged, which can be important for Windows license activation.
Options.boot:
Enables you to specify the boot device order for the VM by assigning one of the device types to each of the four boot device slots that are represented by <N> in the option name.

A value of 1 for <N> represents the first boot device slot, and so on.

The device types are floppy for floppy disks, dvd for DVDs or CDs, disk for hard disks, and net for a network device. A value of none indicates that no boot device is associated with the specified slot.
Options.rtcuseutc: Specifies whether the real-time clock (RTC) uses coordinated universal time (UTC). See section "Motherboard Tab" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.graphicscontroller: Specifies the graphics controller type to use. See section "Screen Tab" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.snapshotfolder: Specifies the name of the VM's snapshot storage folder. If you specify default, the folder name is Snapshots/ in the machine folder.
Options.firmware:
Specifies the firmware used to boot the VM. Valid values are: bios, efi, efi32, or efi64. Use EFI values with care.

By default, BIOS firmware is used.
Options.guestmemoryballoon: Specifies the size of the guest memory balloon. The guest memory balloon is the memory allocated by the Guest Additions from the guest OS and returned to the hypervisor for use by other VMs. Specify <size> in megabytes. The default value is 0 megabytes. See section "Memory Ballooning" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.defaultfrontend: Specifies the default frontend to use when starting the specified VM. If you specify default, the VM is shown in a window on the user's desktop. See "VBoxManage startvm".
Options.vmprocesspriority:
Specifies the priority scheme of the VM process to use when starting the specified VM and while the VM runs.

The following valid values are:

- default – Default process priority determined by the OS. - flat – Assumes a scheduling policy which puts the process at the default priority and with all threads at the same priority. - low – Assumes a scheduling policy which puts the process mostly below the default priority of the host OS. - normal – Assume a scheduling policy which shares the CPU res...
Options.nic:
Configures the network type used by each virtual network card in the VM.

The following valid values correspond to the modes described in section "Introduction to Networking Modes" in chapter 1 of the user manual:

- none – No networking present - null – Not connected to the host system - nat – Use network address translation (NAT) - natnetwork – Use a NAT network - bridged – Use bridged networking - intnet – Use internal networking - hostonly – Use host-only networking - generic – Access rarely...
Options.nictype:
Identifies the type of networking hardware that Oracle VirtualBox presents to the guest VM for the specified virtual network card. See section "Virtual Networking Hardware" in chapter 1 of the user manual.

Valid values are as follows:

- Am79C970A represents the AMD PCNet PCI II. - Am79C973 represents the AMD PCNet FAST III, which is the default value. - 82540EM represents the Intel PRO/1000 MT Desktop. - 82543GC represents the Intel PRO/1000 T Server. - 82545EM represents the Intel PRO/1000 MT...
Options.cableconnected: Temporarily disconnects a virtual network interface, as if you pull a network cable from a physical network card. You might use this option to reset certain software components in the VM.
Options.nictrace: Enables or disables network tracing for the specified virtual network card.
Options.nictracefile: Specifies the absolute path of the file in which to write trace log information. Use this option if network tracing is enabled.
Options.nicproperty:
Enables you to set property values and pass them to rarely used network backends. To use this option, you must also use the --nic-generic-drv option.

These properties are specific to the backend engine and differ between the UDP Tunnel and the VDE backend drivers. For property examples, see section "UDP Tunnel Networking" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.nicspeed: Specifies the throughput rate in kilobits per second for rarely used networking sub-modes such as VDE network and UDP Tunnel. Use this option only if you used the --nic option to enable generic networking for the specified virtual network card.
Options.nicbootprio:
Assigns a priority to each NIC that determines the order in which that NIC is used to perform a PXE network boot. The priority value is an integer in the range from 0 to 4. Priority 0, which is the default value, is the lowest priority. Priority 1 is the highest priority, and priorities 3 and 4 are lower.

This option has an effect only when using the Intel PXE boot ROM.
Options.nicpromisc:
Enables you to specify whether to deny or allow promiscuous mode for the specified VM virtual network card. This option is relevant only for bridged networking. Valid values are as follows:

- deny hides any traffic that is not intended for the VM. This is the default value. - allow-vms hides all host traffic from the VM, but allows the VM to see traffic to and from other VMs. - allow-all allows the VM to see all traffic.
Options.nicbandwidthgroup:
Adds or removes a bandwidth group assignment to the specified virtual network interface. Valid values are as follows:

- none removes any current bandwidth group assignment from the specified virtual network interface. - <name> adds a bandwidth group assignment to the specified virtual network interface.

See section "Limiting Bandwidth for Network Input/Output" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.bridgeadapter: Specifies the host interface to use for the specified virtual network interface. See section "Bridged Networking" in chapter 1 of the user manual. Use this option only if you used the --nic option to enable bridged networking for the specified virtual network card.
Options.hostonlyadapter: Specifies which host-only networking interface to use for the specified virtual network interface. See section "Host-Only Networking" in chapter 1 of the user manual. Use this option only if you used the --nic option to enable host-only networking for the specified virtual network card.
Options.intnet: Specifies the name of the internal network. See section "Internal Networking" in chapter 1 of the user manual. Use this option only if you used the --nic option to enable internal networking for the specified virtual network card.
Options.natnetwork: Specifies the name of the NAT network to which this adapter is connected. Use this option only if the networking type is natnetwork, not nat.
Options.nicgenericdrv: Enables you to access rarely used networking sub-modes, such as VDE networks and UDP Tunnel. Use this option only if you used the --nic option to enable generic networking for a virtual network card.
Options.macaddress: Specifies the MAC address of the specified network adapter on the VM. By default, Oracle VirtualBox assigns a random MAC address to each network adapter at VM creation.
Options.natnet: Specifies the IP address range to use for this network. See section "Fine Tuning the NAT Engine" in chapter 1 of the user manual. Use this option only if the networking type is nat, not natnetwork.
Options.natpf: Specifies the NAT port-forwarding rule to use. See section "Configuring Port Forwarding with NAT" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.nattftpprefix: Specifies a prefix to use for the built-in TFTP server. For example, you might use a prefix to indicate where the boot file is located. See section "PXE Booting with NAT" in chapter 1 of the user manual and section "Configuring the Boot Server (Next Server) of a NAT Network Interface" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.nattftpfile: Specifies the name of the TFT boot file. See section "Configuring the Boot Server (Next Server) of a NAT Network Interface" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.nattftpserver: Specifies the address of the TFTP server from which to boot. See section "Configuring the Boot Server (Next Server) of a NAT Network Interface" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.natbindip: Specifies an alternate IP address to which the NAT engine binds. See section "Fine Tuning the NAT Engine" in chapter 1 of the user manual. By default, Oracle VirtualBox's NAT engine routes TCP/IP packets through the default interface assigned by the host's TCP/IP stack.
Options.natdnspassdomain: Specifies whether the built-in DHCP server passes the domain name for network name resolution.
Options.natlocalhostreachable: Specifies whether the NAT engine allows traffic from the guest directed to 10.0.2.2 to pass to the host's loopback interface, i.e. localhost or 127.0.0.1.
Options.natsettings: Specifies values for tuning NAT performance. See section "Fine Tuning the NAT Engine" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.mouse: Specifies the mode of the mouse to use in the VM. Valid values are: ps2, usb, usbtablet, usbmultitouch and usbmtscreenpluspad.
Options.keyboard: Specifies the mode of the keyboard to use in the VM. Valid values are: ps2 and usb.
Options.uart: Configures virtual serial ports for the VM. <N> represents the serial port to modify. Valid values are off to disable the port or an I/O base address and IRQ. For information about the traditional COM port I/O base address and IRQ values, see section "Serial Ports" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.uartmode:
Specifies how Oracle VirtualBox connects the specified virtual serial port to the host system that runs the VM. See section "Serial Ports" in chapter 1 of the user manual.

Ensure that you first configure the virtual serial port by using the --uart<N> option.

Specify one of the following connection modes for each port:

- disconnected indicates that even though the serial port is shown to the guest VM, it is not connected. This state is like a physical COM port without a cable attached. - serve...
Options.uarttype: Configures the UART type for the specified virtual serial port (<N>). Valid values are 16450, 16550A, and 16750. The default value is 16550A.
Options.lptmode:
Specifies the device name of the parallel port to use.

For a Windows host system, use a device name such as lpt1. For a Linux host system, use a device name such as /dev/lp0.
Options.lpt:
Specifies the I/O base address and IRQ of the parallel port.

You can view the I/O base address and IRQ that the VM uses for the parallel port in the Device Manager.
Options.audiocontroller: Specifies the audio controller to be used with the VM. Valid audio controller type values are: ac97, hda, and sb16.
Options.audiocodec: Specifies the audio codec to be used with the VM. Valid audio codec type values are: stac9700, ad1980, stac9221, and sb16.
Options.audiodriver:
Specifies whether which audio driver (backend) to use. none, default, null, dsound, was, oss, alsa, pulse, and coreaudio.

Note that the audio driver are dependent on the host operating system. Use the VBoxManage modifyvm command usage output to determine the supported audio types for your host system.

For maximum interoperability between hosts, the default audio driver can be used. The VM will then automatically select the most appropriate audio driver for the current host available.
Options.audioenabled:
Specifies whether to enable or disable audio for the VM.

This option has precedence over the --audio-on and --audio-off options, i.e. turning off audio via this option will turn off both, input and output, audio.
Options.audioin: Specifies whether to enable or disable audio capture from the host system.
Options.audioout: Specifies whether to enable or disable audio playback from the guest VM.
Options.clipboard:
Specifies how to share the guest VM or host system OS's clipboard with the host system or guest VM, respectively. Valid values are: disabled, hosttoguest, guesttohost, and bidirectional. See section "General Settings" in chapter 1 of the user manual.

The clipboard feature is available only if you have the Guest Additions be installed in the VM.
Options.clipboardfiletransfers:
Specifies whether file transfers via clipboard between the guest VM and the host are enabled or not. Valid values are: disabled, enabled. Depends on the current clipboard mode being set.

This clipboard file transfer feature is available only if you have the Guest Additions be installed in the VM.
Options.draganddrop:
Specifies how to use the drag and drop feature between the host system and the VM. Valid values are: disabled, hosttoguest, guesttohost, and bidirectional. See section "Drag and Drop" in chapter 1 of the user manual.

The drag and drop feature is available only if you have the Guest Additions be installed in the VM.
Options.monitorcount: Enables you to configure multiple monitors. See section "Display Settings" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.usbohci: Enables or disables the VM's virtual USB 1.1 controller. See section "USB Settings" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.usbehci: Enables or disables the VM's virtual USB 2.0 controller. See section "USB Settings" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.usbxhci: Enables or disables the VM's virtual USB 3.0 controller. This is the most efficient option if the VM supports it. See section "USB Settings" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.usbrename: Rename's the VM's virtual USB controller from <old-name> to <new-name>.
Options.recording: Enables or disables the recording of a VM session into a WebM or VP8 file. When set to on, recording begins when the VM session starts.
Options.recordingscreens: Enables you to specify the VM screens to record. The recording for each screen is output to its own file. Valid values are: all, which records all screens, none, which records no screens, or one or more specified screens.
Options.recordingfile: Specifies the name of the file in which to save the recording.
Options.recordingmaxsize: Specifies the maximum size of the recorded video file in megabytes. When the file reaches the specified size, recording stops. If the value is 0, recording continues until you manually stop recording.
Options.recordingmaxtime: Specifies the maximum amount of time to record in seconds. When the specified time elapses, recording stops. If the value is 0, recording continues until you manually stop recording.
Options.recordingopts:
Specifies additional video-recording properties as a comma-separated property keyword-value list. For example, foo=bar,a=b.

Only use this option if you are an advanced user. For information about keywords, see the Oracle VirtualBox Programming Guide and Reference.
Options.recordingvideofps: Specifies the maximum number of video frames per second (FPS) to record. The recording ignores any frames that have a higher frequency. When you increase the FPS, fewer frames are ignored but the recording and the size of the recording file increases.
Options.recordingvideorate: Specifies the bit rate of the video in kilobits per second. When you increase the bit rate, the recording appearance improves and the size of the recording file increases.
Options.recordingvideores: Specifies the video resolution (width and height) of the recorded video in pixels.
Options.vrde: Enables or disables the VRDE server.
Options.vrdeproperty:
<port> is the port or port range to which the VRDE server binds. The default or 0 value uses port 3389, which is the standard RDP port.

See also the --vrde-port option description.
Options.vrdeextpack:
Specifies the library to use to access the VM remotely. The default value uses the RDP code that is part of the Oracle VirtualBox Extension Pack.

To use the VRDE module in VNC, specify VNC. See section "Other Extension Packs" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.vrdeport:
<port> is the port or port range to which the VRDE server binds. The default or 0 value uses port 3389, which is the standard RDP port.

You can specify a comma-separated list of ports or port ranges of ports. Use a dash between two port numbers to specify a port range. The VRDE server binds to only one of the available ports from the list. Only one machine can use a given port at a time. For example, the --vrde-port=5000,5010-5012 option specifies that server can bind to one of following ports:...
Options.vrdeaddress:
Specifies the IP address of the host network interface to which the VRDE server binds. If you specify an IP address, the server accepts connections only on the specified host network interface.

Use this option to specify whether the VRDP server should accept IPv4, IPv6, or both type of connections:

- Only IPv4: Use the --vrde-address="0.0.0.0" option. - Only IPv6: Use the --vrde-address="::" option. - Both IPv6 and IPv4: Use the --vrde-address="" option. This is the default value.
Options.vrdeauthtype:
Specify whether to use authorization and how to perform authorization. See section "RDP Authentication" in chapter 1 of the user manual. Valid values are as follows:

- null provides no authentication. - external provides external authentication through an authentication library. - guest performs authentication by using guest user accounts. This unsupported method requires that you install the Guest Additions on the VM.
Options.vrdeauthlibrary: Specifies the library to use for RDP authentication. The default library for external authentication is VBoxAuth. See section "RDP Authentication" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.vrdemulticon: Enables or disables the multiple connections VRDE server feature, if supported. See section "Multiple Connections to the VRDP Server" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.vrdereusecon: Specifies how the VRDE server behaves when multiple connections are disabled. When the value is on, the server permits a new client to connect and drops the existing connection. When the value is off, a new connection is not accepted if a client is already connected to the server. This is the default value.
Options.vrdevideochannel: Enables video redirection if supported by the VRDE server. See section "VRDP Video Redirection" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.vrdevideochannelquality: Specifies the image quality for video redirection as a value from 10 to 100 percent. The percentage represents the JPEG compression level where a lower number diminishes quality and provides higher compression. See section "VRDP Video Redirection" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.teleporter:
Enables or disables the teleporter. When enabled, a machine starts up and waits to receive a teleporting request from the network instead of booting normally.

Teleporting requests are received on the port and address specified using the following parameters.
Options.teleporterport: Specifies the port on which the VM listens to receive a teleporting request from another VM. <port> is any free TCP/IP port number, such as 6000. You must also specify the --teleporter option.
Options.teleporteraddress: Specifies the IP address on which the VM listens to receive a teleporting request from another VM. <IP-address> is any IP address or host name and specifies the TCP/IP socket on which to bind. The default IP address is 0.0.0.0, which represents any IP address. You must also specify the --teleporter option.
Options.teleporterpassword: Specifies the password to use for authentication. When specified, the teleporting request only succeeds if the password on the source machine is the same password as the one you specify.
Options.teleporterpasswordfile: Specifies a file that contains the password to use for authentication. When specified, the teleporting request only succeeds if the password on the source machine is the same password as the one you specify in the password file. A value of stdin reads the password from standard input.
Options.cpuidportabilitylevel: Restricts the virtual CPU capabilities that Oracle VirtualBox presents to the guest OS by using portability rules. Higher integer values designate more restrictive behavior. The default level of 0 indicates that all virtualized features supported by the host are made available to the guest. The value 3 suppresses most features. Values of 1 and 2 represent restrictions in between. The behavior may change depending on the product version.
Options.cpuidset: Advanced users can use this setting before a teleporting operation (in fact before starting the VM) to restrict the virtual CPU capabilities that Oracle VirtualBox presents to the guest operating system. This must be run on both the source and the target machines involved in teleporting and will then modify what the guest sees when it executes the CPUID machine instruction. Options.tracingenabled: Enables or disables the trace buffer. Note that when specified, the trace buffer consumes some memory and adds overhead.
Options.tracingconfig: Enables a tracing configuration that defines which group of trace points are enabled.
Options.tracingallowvmaccess: Enables or disables VM access to the trace buffer. The default value is off, which disables access.
Options.usbcardreader: Enables or disables the USB card reader interface.
Options.autostartenabled: Enables or disables VM autostart at host system boot-up for the specified users.
Options.autostartdelay: Specifies the number of seconds after host system boot-up to autostart the VM.
Options.guestdebugprovider: Selects the given debug stub provider.
Options.guestdebugioprovider: Selects the given I/O transport backend for the selected provider.
Options.guestdebugaddress: Sets the path the debugger is accessible under, depends on the selected I/O transport.
Options.guestdebugport: Sets the port the debugger is accessible under, depends on the selected I/O transport.
Options.pciattach: Attaches the specified PCI network controller on the host to the guest VM. You can optionally specify the PCI bus on the guest VM on which to attach the controller.  See <xref linkend="pcipassthrough" />.
Options.pcidetach: Detaches the specified PCI network controller from the attached PCI bus on the guest VM.  See <xref linkend="pcipassthrough" />.
Options.testingenabled: Enabled the testing functionality of the VMMDev. See VMMDevTesting.h for details.
Options.testingmmio: Enabled the MMIO region of the VMMDev testing feature.
Options.testingcfgdword\u003Cidx\u003E: This sets one of the 10 dword configuration values. The <idx> must be in the range 0 through 9. The <value> is limited to 32 bits (dword).

Options.transient: Specifies that the share is transient which means that it is added and removed to a running VM and does not persist after the VM stops.

Options.controller:
Specifies the chipset type to emulate for the specified storage controller. Valid values are BusLogic, I82078, ICH6, IntelAHCI, LSILogic, LSILogicSAS, NVMe, PIIX3, PIIX4, and USB.

The default value varies, according to the type of storage controller.
Options.portcount: Specifies the number of ports that the storage controller supports. Valid values depend on the type of storage controller.
Options.hostiocache: Specifies whether to use the host I/O cache for all disk images attached to this storage controller. Valid values are on and off. See section "Host Input/Output Caching" in chapter 1 of the user manual.
Options.bootable: Specifies whether this controller is bootable. Valid values are on and off.
Options.rename: Specifies a new name for the storage controller.
Options.remove: Removes a storage controller from the VM configuration.

Options.iso: The installation ISO to run the detection on.
Options.machinereadable: Produce output that is simpler to parse from a script.
Options.userpassword: The user login password. This is used for the user given by --user (default: changeme)
Options.userpasswordfile: Alternative to --user-password for providing the user password. Special filename stdin can be used to read the password from standard input.
Options.adminpassword: The admin / root login password. If not specified, the password from --user-password will be used.
Options.adminpasswordfile: Alternative to --admin-password for providing the admin / root password. Special filename stdin can be used to read the password from standard input.
Options.key: The guest OS product key. Not all guest OSes requires this.
Options.installadditions: Whether to install the VirtualBox guest additions. (default: --no-install-additions)
Options.additionsiso: Path to the VirtualBox guest additions ISO. (default: installed/downloaded GAs)
Options.installtxs: Whether to install the Test eXecution Service (TXS) from the VirtualBox ValidationKit. This is useful when preparing VMs for testing or similar. (default: --no-install-txs)
Options.validationkitiso: Path to the VirtualBox ValidationKit ISO. This is required if --install-txs is specified.
Options.locale: The base locale specification for the guest, like en_US, de_CH, or nn_NO. (default: host or en_US)
Options.country: The two letter country code if it differs from the specified by --location.
Options.timezone: The time zone to set up the guest OS with. (default: host time zone or UTC)
Options.hostname: The fully qualified domain name of the guest machine. (default: <vmname>.myguest.virtualbox.org)
Options.packageselectionadjustment: Adjustments to the guest OS packages/components selection. This can be specified more than once. Currently the only recognized keyword is minimal which triggers a minimal installation for some of the guest OSes.
Options.dryrun: Do not create any files or make any changes to the VM configuration.
Options.startvm: Start the VM using the front end given by <session-type>. This is the same as the --type option for the startvm command, but we have add none for indicating that the VM should not be started. (default: none)
Options.auxiliarybasepath: The path prefix to the media related files generated for the installation. (default: <vm-config-dir>/Unattended-<vm-uuid>-)
Options.scripttemplate: The unattended installation script template. (default: IMachine::OSTypeId dependent)
Options.postinstalltemplate: The post installation script template. (default: IMachine::OSTypeId dependent)
Options.postinstallcommand: A single command to run after the installation is completed. The exact format and exactly when this is run is guest OS installer dependent.
Options.extrainstallkernelparameters: List of extra Linux kernel parameters to use during the installation. (default: IMachine::OSTypeId dependent)
Options.language: Specifies the UI language for a Windows installation. The <lang> is generally of the form {ll}-{CC}. See the detectedOSLanguages results from VBoxManage unattended detect. (default: detectedOSLanguages[0])

Options.delete:
Deletes the following files related to the VM automatically:

- All hard disk image files, including differencing files. - All saved state files that the machine created, including one for each snapshot. - XML VM machine definition file and its backups. - VM log files. - The empty directory associated with the unregistered VM.
Options.deleteall: Deletes the files described in the --delete option, as well as all DVDs and Floppy disks located in the VM folder and attached only to this VM.

usbdevsource.Summary: Add and remove USB device sources

Options.address: Specifies the address of the USB backend.
Options.backend:
Specifies the USB proxy service backend to use.

If specifying a remote server over the USB/IP protocol the only currently supported backend value is USBIP.

Options.action: Specifies whether to allow VMs access to devices that match a USB filter (hold) or to deny them access (ignore). This option applies only to global filters.
Options.active: Specifies whether a USB filter is active or temporarily disabled. Valid values are yes, which activates the filter, and no, which disables the filter. The default value is yes.
Options.manufacturer: Specifies a manufacturer ID filter as a string. The default value is an empty string ("").
Options.maskedinterfaces: Specifies a masked interface filter that is used to hide one or more USB interfaces from the guest. The value is a bit mask where the set bits correspond to the USB interfaces to hide, or mask off. This feature is supported on Linux host systems only.
Options.name: Specifies the name of the filter.
Options.port: Specifies a hub port number filter as a string. The default value is an empty string ("").
Options.product: Specifies a product ID filter as a string. The default value is an empty string ("").
Options.productid: Specifies a product ID filter. The string representation for an exact match has the form <XXXX>, where <X> is a hexadecimal digit including leading zeroes. The default value is an empty string ("").
Options.remote: Specifies a remote filter that indicates whether the device is physically connected to a remote VRDE client or to a local host system. This option applies to VM filters only. The default value is no.
Options.revision:
Specifies a revision ID filter. The string representation for an exact match has the form <IIFF>. <I> is a decimal digit of the integer part of the revision. <F> is a decimal digit of its fractional part that includes leading and trailing zeros. The default value is an empty string ("").

To specify a range of revision IDs, ensure that you use the hexadecimal form so that the revision is stored as a 16-bit packed BCD value. For example, the int:0x0100-0x0199 expression matches any revision from...
Options.serialnumber: Specifies a serial number filter as a string. The default value is an empty string ("").
Options.target: Specifies the VM that the filter is attached to. You can specify the Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) or the name of the VM. To apply the filter description to all VMs, specify global.
Options.vendorid: Specifies a vendor ID filter, which is a string representation of a four-digit hexadecimal number. <X> is the hexadecimal digit including leading zeroes. The default value is an empty string ("").

vboximg-mount.Summary: FUSE mount a virtual disk image (Linux and macOS hosts only)

Options.image: The UUID, name or path of the VirtualBox disk image. Short form: -i.
Options.guestfilesystem: Enables experimental read-only support for guest file systems (FAT, NTFS, ext2, ext3, ext4). Short form: -g.
Options.o: FUSE mount options, as described in the mount.fuse(8) man page.
Options.root: Also grants file access to the root user. Same as -o allow_root. Incompatible with -o allow_other.
Options.rw: Mounts the image read-write. By default images are mounted read-only.
Options.list: Shows the disks of registered VMs, or the partitions of the given image. Short form: -l.
Options.verbose: Shows detailed information, including snapshot images and file paths. Short form: -v.
Options.vm: Shows information about the VM with this UUID.
Options.wide: Wide output, including the lock state of running VMs and the snapshot tree.

Titles.vboximg-mount: Mount or list a disk image
